basics.name: Oscar Jaroker
basics.label: Undergraduate Student
basics.summary: My academic preparation includes knowledge of computational mathematics and numerical methods, research experience in combinatorics, and competition experience in math modeling and data analysis. Some of my academic projects include mathematical simulations using MATLAB, Simulink, and R programming.  My academic and professional goals are to work in the fields of physics and engineering.

education.area: Applied Mathematics and Physics with Coursework in Computer Science

work.name: Colgate University
work.summary: Designing and building remote sensing devices
highlights: Assembling and improving AQUA-Flux, a low-cost autonomous floating chamber for long-term monitoring of CH4 & CO2 gas fluxes in wetlands
Using Arduino to facilitate actuator movement and data collection via I2C sensors

work.name: Art of Problem Solving
work.summary: TA for Middle School Science Contest class.
highlights: Led hands-on demonstrations and experiments in optics, circuits, and magnetism for a 15-hour/week middle school Science Olympiad class
Guided 18 students through complex concepts and problem-solving, fostering collaboration and critical thinking
Prepared and organized all materials, ensuring smooth execution of lessons and Olympiad practice

work.name: Pfizer Corporate Treasury
work.summary: Financial modeling and analysis of corporate treasury operations.
highlights: Conducted financial research of pharmaceutical industry by coding drug-industry benchmarking program, accessing Bloomberg data through Python API, to compare key company metrics across peer groups
Simulated and reproduced S&P/Moody's credit rating of Pfizer debt to understand the credit rating process
Developed pricing simulator for interest-rate swaps using Bloomberg API and R programming language to understand how interest rate movements might affect Pfizer’s portfolio

Presented results through multiple PowerPoint presentations to Capital Markets, Capital Strategy, Risk Management groups to show how company metrics and potential movements could impact future strategy

projects.name: Optimal Harvesting in Stochastic Predator-Prey Environment
highlights: Applying stochastic control to find optimal harvesting in 2-species fishery following highly nonlinear dynamics
Using MATLAB to implement numerical methods such as FB Sweep, Euler-Maruyama, Backward Euler

projects.name: Data Analysis of "Allentown": Measuring Musical Influence
highlights: Conducted analysis of the song “Allentown”, a collaboration between 3 bands, answering the questions of which band(s) had the greatest influence on the lyrics and music in the song
Utilized R to clean and summarize the data and perform various analyses, including t-tests and bootstrap analysis
Communicated results clearly in a written report, including visualizations and explanations
